title: PR Velocity Oracle — CI oracle for tokens/sec and p95 regression detection
creator: Aisha Kline
description:
Problem: PRs that change runtime scheduling, batching or kernel selection occasionally introduce subtle throughput or p95 regressions that slip past unit tests but surface in production. We need a CI-side oracle that automatically evaluates PRs for regression risk on tokens/sec and p95 across realistic slices, and gates merges when risk exceeds configurable thresholds.

Scope: Build a 'Velocity Oracle' service integrated into PR pipelines that: (1) selects representative baseline slices for the affected model(s) and sequence-length distributions, (2) runs lightweight microbenchmarks (synthetic and sampled traces) to estimate tokens/sec and p95 distributions for the PR vs baseline, (3) applies a statistical risk model (mixture of robust change detection + Bayesian posterior predictive checks) to decide pass/warn/fail gates, and (4) emits structured artifacts (benchmarks, traces, diff dashboards, and suggested mitigations).

Out of scope: full end-to-end multi-region load testing in this ticket (follow-up), integrating Dedicated autoscaler heuristics, and long-running soak tests (>1 hour).
acceptance_criteria: CI job runs Velocity Oracle for any PR touching runtime or kernel selection code paths
Oracle computes tokens/sec and p95 distributions for PR and baseline across 3 sequence-length buckets (short, medium, long)
Oracle returns a Pass/Warn/Fail decision and an explainable rationale included in PR checks
Artifacts (raw bench traces, summary metrics, visual diff link) are uploaded to the perf dashboard and a GitHub check is created
False positive rate should be < 4% on historical regression-free PRs (measured during validation window)
End-to-end CI job completes within 20 minutes for typical PRs (configurable fast-mode/slow-mode)
Configuration knobs exist for threshold tuning, sample size, and baseline selection strategy
design_notes: Baseline selection: keep rolling baseline snapshot (last 7 days stable merges) plus a pinned canonical commit for reproducibility
Stratification: 3 buckets by sequence length (<=128, 129-1024, >1024) and model variant tag (quantized vs fp16)
Statistical engine: combine robust median-of-means for throughput with Bayesian posterior predictive checks for p95 tail shifts; compute risk score as weighted sum with explainable contribs
Noise control: use paired-test protocol when PR and baseline run on same ephemeral runner to reduce runner variance; if not paired, apply runner-variance inflation factor
Synthetic microbursts: include short microburst workloads to expose queuing/queue-thrashing regressions missed by steady-state tests
Resource isolation: run benchmarks in small isolated GCP project to reduce noisy neighbor flakiness during validation run
implementation_plan: 1) Implement lightweight runner harness that accepts benchmark slice descriptor and returns JSON summary (tokens/sec histogram, p95 samples, run metadata)
2) Integrate harness into CI as a reusable job template (github actions + internal runner pool)
3) Implement Velocity Oracle service that selects baseline slices, triggers harness runs for PR and baseline, aggregates results and applies statistical model
4) Produce GitHub check outcome with structured JSON artifact and link to perf dashboard
5) Validation: run Oracle against last 30 days of merged PRs to measure false positive/negative rates and calibrate thresholds
6) Rollout: enable as Warn-only for runtime area (2 weeks), then block merges on Fail if thresholds stable
test_plan: Unit tests for harness parsing, histogram merging, and statistical routines
Replay tests: replay recorded production traces to ensure oracle detects injected regressions at expected sensitivity
Historical simulation: run oracle over 90-day merging window and measure gating accuracy vs known incidents
A/B validation: route a subset of PRs through oracle in shadow mode and compare to current manual perf reviews
Load safety: throttle concurrent CI harness runs to keep runner pool healthy; add circuit breaker for elevated transient noise
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (shadow): 1 week against runtime repo only, record outcomes but do not block
Phase 1 (warn): 2 weeks, post check with human-approved override; collect feedback from eng leads
Phase 2 (block): enable Fail gating for PRs touching critical runtime packages with on-call escalation playbook
Rollback: disable oracle gate and revert commit in case of systemic false-positive pattern; we keep audit logs for 30 days
comments: 2026-02-11 - Aisha Kline: Spiked a PoC harness that runs 3 short synthetic workloads. Latency variance was ~8% on our dev runners; pairing runs on same runner reduced variance to ~2%.
2026-02-18 - Marco Chen: Chose Bayesian PPC for p95 because standard parametric tests were too brittle on heavy-tailed samples. Will implement with Stan-lite (lightweight) or Pyro micro-models.
2026-03-01 - Design review: PM and Observability recommended adding a rerun-if-noisy strategy and a run-level variance score in the artifact so reviewers can triage flaky results faster.
2026-03-05 - QA: Found an edge-case where quantized kernels on a runner with mixed GPUs produce outlier throughput; added runner-tagging to ensure baseline compatibility.

2026-03-12 - Marco Chen: Implemented baseline snapshot rotation and initial GitHub check integration; current false-positive on historical sim = 3.7% (within target). Next: dashboard links and warn-mode rollout
